description: PlanetCam UPV/EHU is a lucky-imaging camera for Solar System studies. Its two-channel configuration simultaneously images visible and short-wave infrared light through broad- and narrow-band filters.
short_description: PlanetCam UPV/EHU lucky-imaging camera visible and SWIR filters
facility_description: Calar Alto Observatory is located in the Sierra de Filabres in Almería, Spain, and is jointly operated by IAA-CSIC and the Andalusian Government.
notes: CAHA describes PlanetCam as owned by the UPV/EHU planetary-sciences group and available through collaboration. That observing restriction is not itself a curve licence; no explicit numerical-filter redistribution grant found on the CAHA instrument page or the owner university article. NJM PlanetCam2 is treated as the two-channel configuration, without asserting each response variant is characterised by the instrument paper. Research accessed 2026-10-26. General CAHA observing acknowledgement is conditional on observational data and a proposal identifier; no observing proposal or SVO use is invented for these filter curves. Rights checked against CAHA legal notice (https://www.caha.es/es/?option=com_content&view=article&id=14725) and data management plan (https://www.caha.es/joomlaCMS/images/docs/DMPlan-CAHA.pdf); neither establishes an unambiguous grant for these third-party filter files.
